tradeoffs.loses: the best-effort seed=0 reproducibility hint on routed OpenAI requests (Router's Responses API rejects seed)
tradeoffs.why: Every gpt/o-series call in llm.py sends seed=0, which the runtime cannot translate, so all of them stayed on OpenAI. OpenAI never guaranteed determinism from seed and these calls run at temperature 0.75, so no reproducibility that exists today is lost.

tradeoffs.loses: the best-effort seed=0 reproducibility hint on routed OpenAI requests (Router's Responses API rejects seed)
tradeoffs.why: Same trade-off for the ensemble entry point get_batch_responses_from_llm.

tradeoffs.loses: the exact Claude 3.5 Sonnet 2024 weights: Router's catalog does not carry them, so these calls are served by claude-sonnet-5 and will answer differently
tradeoffs.why: claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 is the app's default --model and is not in Router's catalog, so the whole Claude path stayed on Anthropic. claude-sonnet-5 is the nearest current Sonnet and is cheaper than the 2024 model it replaces ($2/$10 vs $3/$15 per 1M).

tradeoffs.loses: the exact May-2024 gpt-4o snapshot: Router's catalog carries only the undated gpt-4o, so the paper reviewer is served by a newer snapshot and will score differently
tradeoffs.why: launch_scientist.py and launch_oe_scientist.py hardcode model=gpt-4o-2024-05-13 for every paper review; that dated id is not in Router's catalog (Router maps gpt-4o-2024-08-06 to gpt-4o but not -05-13), so the whole review stage stayed on OpenAI. gpt-4o is the same family at half the input price ($2.50 vs $5 per 1M).
